NC-2025-HB116.aiSummary: The law adds certain parts of Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, Marine Corps Air Station New River, and Marine Corps Special Operations Command at Stones Bay and the New River to the City of Jacksonville. It says these areas will be subject to city taxes for tax years starting on or after July 1, 2026, and it limits the city’s power to regulate federal activities at those bases. It also changes where Jacksonville police can use arrest powers and says the city may not annex land south of N.C. Highway 24 or use city land-use powers outside its contiguous city limits.

NC-2025-HR1245.title: Honor 250th Anniversary and NC's Role.
NC-2025-HR1245.policyArea: AWARDS, HONORS & MEMORIALS; CALENDAR; CULTURAL RESOURCES; GENERAL ASSEMBLY; HOLIDAYS & OBSERVANCES; RESOLUTIONS, SIMPLE
NC-2025-HR1245.aiSummary: This resolution honors the 250th anniversary of the United States and North Carolina’s role in the nation’s founding. It recognizes the state’s history, including the Halifax Resolves and the Mecklenburg Resolves, and honors North Carolinians who served in the Revolutionary War. It also encourages people in North Carolina to take part in events marking the 250th anniversary.

NC-2025-SB355.aiSummary: The law makes changes to adult correction work and related court rules in North Carolina. It expands tuition waivers for some survivors and family members of certain public safety workers, updates rules for electronic and satellite-based monitoring, and changes how the Post-Release Supervision and Parole Commission makes some decisions. It also changes how sexually violent predator reviews are done, raises the yearly limit on some purchases from Correction Enterprises to $4,000, and adds more authority for the Department of Adult Correction on substance abuse assessments.

NC-2025-HB372.aiSummary: Cities in North Carolina would not be allowed to ban certain low-impact home-based businesses or require permits, licenses, or similar approvals for them. These businesses must be run from a home, stay mostly inside or in the yard, not cause much traffic or street parking, and follow state and federal law. The law also says cities cannot require rezoning to commercial use or fire sprinklers just for these businesses, but homeowners association rules and deed limits still apply.

NC-2025-HB1094.aiSummary: This act became law and makes several changes for the City of Durham. It lets Durham set a lower default speed limit of at least 20 miles per hour on city streets that are not part of the state highway system, with gateway signs and a public map. It also sets faster review steps for Durham requests to change speed limits on state highways. The act includes a technical fix for motor vehicle dealer rules, with that part set to take effect on October 1, 2026.

NC-2025-HB600.aiSummary: The bill would give official state recognition to The Tuscarora Indians of Kahtenuaka Territories starting July 1, 2026. It would also add two Tuscarora members to the State Commission of Indian Affairs and one Tuscarora representative to the American Indian Heritage Commission. The bill sets aside $5,000 for the Department of Administration and $5,000 for Natural and Cultural Resources to update websites and other materials.

NC-2025-HB1083.aiSummary: The bill would create a voluntary portable benefits account system for independent contractors. Hiring parties could put money into these accounts, but the worker would have to agree in writing and could opt out at any time. The money could be used for things like health coverage, retirement savings, disability insurance, and life insurance, and the bill sets tax rules and reporting rules for these accounts. It would take effect January 1, 2027, and apply to tax years starting on or after that date.
